title: Macbeth
author: William Shakespeare
note: Wikipedia: first printed in the 1623 First Folio; generally dated/first performed 1606 (written 1599-1606 per one publisher blurb). Library's 1606 is performance/writing date, not print.
resolution: The library gives the usual date of first performance (1606); the first printing is the 1623 First Folio. Plays are dated by performance or composition; see the README.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
note: Wikipedia: serialised in All the Year Round 1 Dec 1860-Aug 1861; 3-vol book (Chapman & Hall) 1861 (Oct, or Jul per title page). Library's 1861 = book edition; first appearance was 1860.
resolution: The library gives the book edition (1861); the serial began in December 1860. Left as is; see the README note on serials.

title: Iliad
author: Homer
note: Articles (History News Network, The Collector): 8th c. BCE consensus; a genetic study gives c. 762 BCE +/-50; a minority argue 7th c. c. 750 BCE sits in the range. Composition date; oral first.

title: Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell
author: Susanna Clarke
note: Wikipedia and bookseller first-edition listings: Bloomsbury, 2004 (US 8 Sep, UK 30 Sep 2004); Clarke's debut novel.

title: Metamorphoses
author: Ovid
note: Wikipedia infobox 'First published in: 8 CE' (traditional dating of composition/circulation); first printed edition 1471, first English translation 1480.

title: Odyssey
author: Homer
note: Wikipedia: composed around the 8th or 7th century BCE, after the Iliad; Taplin dates Homer c. 750-650 BCE. c. 700 BCE sits in the stated range.

title: Romeo and Juliet
author: William Shakespeare
note: Search results: first quarto 1597 (John Danter, 'bad' quarto), 2nd quarto 1599; written early 1590s (1591-96). Library's 1595 is a composition date, consistent; first publication was 1597.
resolution: The library gives a composition date (about 1595); the first quarto is 1597. Plays are dated by performance or composition; see the README.

title: Solaris
author: Stanisław Lem
note: Wikipedia and a dealer listing: Polish original, Warsaw, MON, 1961; English translation (via French) 1970.

title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
author: C. S. Lewis
note: Wikipedia: first published UK 16 Oct 1950 by Geoffrey Bles, illustrated by Pauline Baynes; US edition (Macmillan) later in 1950.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
note: Several encyclopedia/library pages: first published 19 Dec 1843 by Chapman & Hall, illustrated by John Leech; written Oct-Nov 1843.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
note: History.com and bibliographic pages: serialised in All the Year Round 30 Apr-26 Nov 1859; Chapman & Hall book edition 1859 (one source: 21 Nov).

title: Aeneid
author: Virgil
note: Univ. and publisher pages: Virgil worked on it from c. 29/30 BCE until his death in 19 BCE; published after his death by his executors. c. 19 BCE is death/publication point, not composition.

title: Heimskringla
author: Snorri Sturluson
sourceAuthor: Snorri Sturluson (attributed; not named in the manuscripts)
note: Wikipedia: authorship nowhere stated; scholars assume Snorri, c. 1230. Gutenberg c. 1230; EBSCO 1230-1235. Year consistent; author is a scholarly attribution. Oldest manuscript c. 1260.
resolution: The record already says "traditional attribution"; the author is a scholarly assumption.

title: The Khamsa of Navoi
author: Ali-Shir Navoi
note: Library gives no year, so nothing to contradict. UN Uzbekistan, Royal Collection Trust and BL pages: five masnavis composed 1483-85 in Chagatai; Royal Collection copy dated 1492.

title: Moving Mars
author: Greg Bear
note: Wikipedia and EBSCO: Tor Books, 1993 (BookBrainz: November 1993); won the 1994 Nebula Award for Best Novel.

title: The Pursuit of Love
author: Nancy Mitford
note: Wikipedia and first-edition dealer listings: Hamish Hamilton, London, 1945 (10 Dec 1945 per Airmail); first of a trilogy.

title: Condorito
author: Pepo (René Ríos Boettiger)
note: Tebeosfera and El Nuevo Diario: character first appeared 6 Aug 1949 in Chilean magazine Okey (Zig-Zag). Condorito magazine began 1955. Real name not shown in the results I saw.

title: The Colossus and Other Poems
author: Sylvia Plath
note: Wikipedia and rare-book dealers: UK, Heinemann, 31 Oct 1960 (500 copies); US edition Knopf 14 May 1962.

title: Arcadia
author: Christopher Reid
note: Encyclopedia.com: Arcadia, London and New York, Oxford University Press, 1979; British Council and T. S. Eliot Prize site call it his first collection (1979).

title: The Beautiful Ones Are Not Yet Born
author: Ayi Kwei Armah
note: Wikipedia/Oxford podcast: first published 1968 (Houghton Mifflin), Heinemann AWS 1969. NOTE: the real title is spelled 'The Beautyful Ones Are Not Yet Born'; the library's spelling differs.

title: Not I
author: Samuel Beckett
note: Wikipedia: written 1972, premiered Lincoln Center, New York, Nov 1972 (22 Nov per Knowlson; sources vary). Publication year not shown in results, so 1972 is writing/performance.

title: Mémoires d'Hadrien (Memoirs of Hadrian)
author: Marguerite Yourcenar
note: Wikipedia/Britannica-type pages: first published in France 1951 by Plon; English edition 1954 (US FSG edition 1963 per one source; unresolved).

title: Bilgames and Huwawa (Sumerian Gilgamesh poems)
author: Anonymous
sourceYear: oral origin c. 2100 BCE (Ur III); surviving copies 1900-1600 BCE
note: Met essay and Penn Museum tablets show 'Gilgamesh and Huwawa' copies, Old Babylonian 1900-1600 BCE. No result used the title 'Bilgames' or stated anonymity (my inference). Library gives no year.

title: Welcome to Our Hillbrow
author: Phaswane Mpe
note: Wikipedia and a library catalogue: first published 2001 by University of Natal Press, South Africa; Mpe's only published novel. Ohio University Press edition 2011.

title: Berlin Alexanderplatz
author: Alfred Döblin
note: Britannica entry names Döblin and 1929; Goodreads (1 Oct 1929) and BookBrainz also say first published 1929. Encyclopedia plus catalogue sites.

title: House of Leaves
author: Mark Z. Danielewski
note: Wikipedia/BookBrowse/Goodreads: Pantheon, debut novel, 2000 (Goodreads 29 Feb 2000; Wikipedia and BookBrowse 7 Mar 2000). Sources differ only on the day.

title: Lazarillo de Tormes
author: Anonymous
note: Wikipedia/PRH/Gutenberg: anonymous 1554 editions (Alcalá, Burgos, Medina del Campo, Antwerp; one source puts Antwerp in 1555). Authorship disputed (Ortega, Hurtado de Mendoza guesses).

title: Hatchet
author: Gary Paulsen
note: Wikipedia summary: first published September 1987 by Bradbury Press; rare-book dealer listing also gives first printing Sept 1987.

title: Le Morte d'Arthur
author: Thomas Malory
note: Reference pages: Caxton printed it 1485 (first publication, posthumous); Malory finished text c.1469-70. 1485 = printing, not writing. Author identity debated.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
note: History.com and Wikipedia: vol. 1 published 30 Sept 1868 by Roberts Brothers; vol. 2 (Good Wives in UK) followed in 1869.

title: Ramcharitmanas
author: Tulsidas
note: Britannica: written 1574-1576/77; most sources say begun 1574 (VS 1631), one essay says 1575. Library's c.1574/c.1575 fits; sources disagree on start year.

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
note: Wikipedia: first published in Australia 2005 (Picador); US edition (Knopf) 2006, UK 2007. Library year is the Australian first edition.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
note: Search summary (Wikipedia-derived, dealer): first appeared in Lippincott's Monthly Magazine, June/July 1890; revised book edition (Ward, Lock) 1891. Library year is the magazine debut.

title: The Rape of the Lock
author: Alexander Pope
note: Wikisource/Britannica-based results: first appeared May 1712 as two cantos in Lintot's Miscellany; five-canto separate edition March 1714; final text 1717.

title: The Sparrow
author: Mary Doria Russell
note: Wikipedia and Goodreads: debut novel, Villard, New York, first published 9 Sept 1996.

title: The Temple
author: George Herbert
note: Several pages (Penguin, university and Herbert society pages): published by Cambridge University 1633, shortly after Herbert's death, arranged by Nicholas Ferrar.

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H. G. Wells
note: Wikipedia/Britannica: serialised in Pearson's and Cosmopolitan 1897; book by Heinemann Jan 1898. Library 1898 = book edition; strictly first publication was the 1897 serial.

title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
note: Wikipedia and others: George M. Hill, Chicago, 1900 (17 May first copy off press; official release 1 Sept 1900). Only an audiobook listing says 1901.

title: Things Fall Apart
author: Chinua Achebe
note: Wikipedia and Britannica: Heinemann, London, 17 June 1958. Some pages say 1962, which is the African Writers Series edition, not the first.

title: Uncle Tom's Cabin
author: Harriet Beecher Stowe
note: Wikipedia/History.com: book by John P. Jewett 20 March 1852; first ran as a serial in The National Era from 5 June 1851. Library 1852 = book edition.

title: Winesburg, Ohio
author: Sherwood Anderson
note: Wikipedia and Library of America: B. W. Huebsch, New York, 8 May 1919; some stories had appeared earlier in magazines.

title: A Book of Nonsense
author: Edward Lear
note: EBSCO/Britannica summaries: first appeared 1846 under the name 'Old Derry down Derry'; expanded edition 1861.

title: A Canticle for Leibowitz
author: Walter M. Miller Jr.
note: Wikipedia and library records: J. B. Lippincott, October 1959 (fix-up of magazine stories). Some Bookmate pages say 1960; treated as outliers.

title: A Dictionary of the English Language
author: Samuel Johnson
note: Wikipedia, History Today, EBSCO: first edition 1755 (15 April per most; a dealer says on sale 14 June 1755).

title: Les Trois Mousquetaires (The Three Musketeers)
author: Alexandre Dumas
note: Wikipedia: serialised in Le Siecle March-July 1844, book form July 1844. Co-written with ghostwriter Auguste Maquet.

title: Tango
author: Sławomir Mrożek
note: Wikipedia and Slovenian pages: published 1964 in the magazine Dialog. Premiere 21 April 1965 (Bydgoszcz per Wikipedia; Belgrade per others). Library year = publication.

title: Motif-Index of Folk-Literature
author: Stith Thompson
note: Wikipedia: original edition 1932-1936, revised and enlarged six volumes 1955-1958. Library 1932 = start of the first edition; Goodreads dates 1958 are the revised edition.

title: Poems
author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
note: Rossetti Archive (University of Virginia): Poems, F. S. Ellis, London, April 1870, his first collection of original poetry; privately printed trial editions 1869-70 preceded it.

title: Nothing
author: Henry Green
note: EBSCO summary and Goodreads/review blogs: Henry Green's penultimate novel, published 1950 (Viking Press US edition listed); UK first-edition publisher not shown in results.

title: Sarada kinenbi (Salad Anniversary)
author: Machi Tawara
note: French-language biography and the Pushkin Press edition's author note: first collection Sarada Kinenbi published 1987, a bestseller. Month and Japanese publisher not shown.

title: Los ríos profundos
author: José María Arguedas
note: Wikipedia (Deep Rivers) and Goodreads: Editorial Losada, Buenos Aires, 1958. Two low-quality pages say 1953; disregarded.

title: Encyclopedia Brown, Boy Detective
author: Donald J. Sobol
note: Wikipedia, Encyclopedia.com and a blog: Sobol's first Encyclopedia Brown book, 1963. Original publisher is reported inconsistently (Thomas Nelson vs Penguin); not checked.

title: Taxi Driver
author: Paul Schrader
note: AFI/Wikipedia/MoMA: Schrader wrote the screenplay of the 1976 Scorsese film; script written 1972, optioned 1973. Library 1976 = film release; no screenplay-book date shown.

title: Così fan tutte (libretto)
author: Lorenzo Da Ponte
note: Wikipedia: Da Ponte's libretto, Mozart opera premiered 26 Jan 1790, Burgtheater; Mozarteum catalogue records a printed 1790 Vienna libretto.

title: Menaechmi
author: Plautus
note: Wikipedia and classics abstracts: never securely dated; late 3rd c. BCE, proposals 215-186 BCE, some favour just after 201 BCE. c. 200 BCE sits inside this range, accepted per brief.

title: Façade
author: Michael Mateas and Andrew Stern
note: Wikipedia and eliterature.org: interactive drama released as freeware 5 July 2005 by Procedural Arts; AIIDE 2005 paper; about five years in development.

title: A Farewell to Arms
author: Ernest Hemingway
note: Search summary (bookseller/library listings): serialized in Scribner's Magazine May-Oct 1929, book from Scribner's Sept 1929. Consistent with 1929.

title: A Princess of Mars
author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
sourceYear: 1912 (serial, All-Story, Feb-Jul as 'Under the Moons of Mars'); 1917 (first book)
note: Search summary: 1912 six-part serial in All-Story under the title Under the Moons of Mars; first book edition McClurg Oct 1917. Library 1912 matches first publication (serial), not the book.

title: A Study in Scarlet
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
note: Wikipedia via search: first published Dec 1887 in Beeton's Christmas Annual; Ward Lock book edition July 1888. 1887 is magazine first publication; a 1888 book date is also common.

title: Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl
author: Harriet Jacobs
sourceAuthor: Linda Brent (pseudonym), ed. Lydia Maria Child
note: Search summary (Wikipedia/Encyclopedia.com) confirms 1861, 'under the pseudonym Linda Brent'; the text I saw did not name Jacobs. From memory: Jacobs is the author. Year not in doubt.

title: Island of the Blue Dolphins
author: Scott O'Dell
note: Wikipedia and a rare-book dealer (o-dell-scott listing) give Houghton Mifflin, Boston, 1960; Goodreads gives 9 Sept 1960. Newbery Medal 1961.

title: Kitchen Confidential
author: Anthony Bourdain
note: Wikipedia and bookseller first-edition listings: Bloomsbury, 2000 (Aug 2000 per Wikipedia; 22 May 2000 per a seller). Grew from his 1999 New Yorker article.

title: Poetics
author: Aristotle
note: Search summary (Wikipedia-derived, Pressbooks/Gutenberg hits): c. 335 BCE is the standard composition date; a writing date, not a publication date.

title: Possession
author: A. S. Byatt
note: Wikipedia plus bookseller and library listings: first published 1990 by Chatto & Windus (London); US edition Random House 1990; won 1990 Booker Prize.

title: Psycho
author: Robert Bloch
note: Wikipedia: US edition Simon & Schuster (Inner Sanctum) 10 April 1959. Booksellers differ on UK Robert Hale edition (1959 or 1960); US 1959 undisputed.

title: Red Mars
author: Kim Stanley Robinson
note: Wikipedia infobox: Sept 1992; booksellers: UK HarperCollins 1992, US Spectra edition listed as 1993. Won BSFA 1992, Nebula 1993.

title: Songs and Sonnets
author: John Donne
note: Britannica, Glasgow Univ. Library: poems first collected and printed 1633, posthumously. Memory, not in results: 1633 volume titled 'Poems'; 'Songs and Sonnets' is a later grouping.

title: Station Eleven
author: Emily St. John Mandel
note: Wikipedia: published 9 Sept 2014 (Canada/US), 10 Sept UK. One dealer claims the UK Picador edition came first; that is the only source saying so.

title: The Frogs
author: Aristophanes
note: Wikipedia and other pages: staged at the Lenaia in Athens in 405 BC, won first prize. Consistent with c. 405 BCE (first performance).

title: The Grapes of Wrath
author: John Steinbeck
note: Wikipedia, UVA bibliographic record, rare-book dealers: Viking Press, April 1939 (copyright page 'First Published in April 1939'). One NCTE blog says March; likely error.

title: The Lies of Locke Lamora
author: Scott Lynch
note: Wikipedia: first published 27 June 2006 (Bantam Spectra US, Gollancz UK). Goodreads work page says June 2006. Consistent.

title: The Lottery
author: Shirley Jackson
note: Wikipedia, EBSCO research starter, CSMonitor: first published in The New Yorker, 26 June 1948. One Goodreads page says June 28; most agree on 26 June.

title: The Man of Mode
author: George Etherege
note: Cambridge Orlando, Wikipedia, EMBTA record, Morgan Library: first staged probably 11 March 1676 at the Duke's Theatre; first edition printed 1676 (licensed 3 June). Performance and print same year.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
note: Wikipedia infobox: Sept 2011 self-published (blog serial, then Kindle); Crown print edition Feb 2014. Library's 2011 matches first publication, not the 2014 print edition.
